note: The AS2 MovieClip.attachMovie handler. Unnamed as sub_9FF990; pinned by the AS2 MovieClip method table, whose "attachMovie" name pointer sits immediately before this function pointer, and by its own body - the three LogScriptWarning strings are the attachMovie ones. Resolved by hand: 0x009ff990..0x009ffca7. Reads arg 3 with GASValue::ToObjectInterface and passes it to GFxSprite::AddDisplayObject as the fourth parameter, which is the shape MCAttachMovie now has. Also proves the depth convention: it places at AS depth + 0x4000

GFxSprite::AddDisplayObject, named in the 2012 database, resolved by hand to 0x009fee10..0x009ff98d. In the registered-class arm it queues four action-queue entries - priority 1 __proto__, then at priority 3 the onConstruct event, the init object's members, and the class function - which is what makes the constructor run LAST and is the whole basis of this package. Our port's equivalent is GFxSprite::AttachMovie plus BindRegisteredClass
The GASGlobalContext::FindRegisteredClass call site inside GFxSprite::AddDisplayObject that opens the registered-class arm. Mid-function by intent; cited only to locate the arm

The priority-1 queue handler AddDisplayObject installs. Unnamed as sub_9FB170; its whole body is GASValue::ToFunction followed by GFxASCharacter::SetProtoToPrototypeOf. It is NOT the constructor, which is the misreading that gives the opposite answer about the ordering

The priority-3 queue handler that copies attachMovie's init object onto the clip. Unnamed as sub_9F61B0; pinned by the vftable it installs, `GFx_InitObjectMembers'::`2'::InitVisitor, and by its one visitor call through the object interface. Ported here as the Copier in GFxSprite::AttachMovie

GFx_FindClassAndInitializeClassInstance, named in the 2012 database. The inline twin of the queued path: __proto__, then the onConstruct event, then the class function executed directly. Confirms the same order from a second site. Not ported; nothing in this tree reaches GFxButtonCharacter::RecreateCharacters yet

GFxMovieRoot::ActionQueueIterator::getNext, named. Walks the priority lists from index 0 UPWARD to 5 and restarts at 0 whenever the queue's insert counter changes. This is what fixes the drain order the table above depends on
GFxMovieRoot::ActionQueueType::InsertEntry, named. Appends after a per-priority insert cursor, so entries at one priority run FIFO - the other half of the drain order

The AS2 duplicateMovieClip handler, unnamed as sub_9F5210, pinned by the same method table. CloneDisplayObject at AS depth + 0x4000. Ours (GASop_DuplicateClip) SUBTRACTS 16384. Hand-over, not changed here
GFxASCharacter::CharacterGetDepth, named. Returns the internal depth minus 0x4000. Ours returns it raw. Hand-over, not changed here
The AS2 getNextHighestDepth handler, unnamed as sub_9F5510, pinned by the method table. Returns max(0, GetLargestDepthInUse - 0x3FFF). Ours returns largest + 1 raw. Hand-over, not changed here

The AS2 removeMovieClip handler, unnamed as sub_9F6C00, pinned by the method table. Refuses unless the internal depth is >= 0x4000. Agent EZ's bScriptCreated flag stands in for it. Hand-over, not changed here

The AS2 setMask handler, unnamed as sub_9F5320, pinned by the method table. Not in our AS2 MovieClip table at all; the options list raises 'call of a value that is not a function: setMask' twice per open. Does not block the options screen or its footer bar with this package applied

GFxSprite::ExecuteFrame0Events, named. Runs ExecuteFrameTags(0) inline and queues the Load event at priority 5 - after everything AddDisplayObject queued. Unchanged by this package; the init-object copy is placed after our call to it, which is the smallest change the binary justifies
